sections.title: The Flying Scroll
observations: In this vision, Zechariah sees a flying scroll that measures 20 cubits by 10 cubits, symbolizing God's judgment against sin.
The scroll contains a curse that will go out over the whole land, indicating that God's judgment is not limited to a specific group but encompasses all who transgress His laws.
The dimensions of the scroll suggest a significant message, as it is large enough to be seen and understood by all.

sections.title: The Woman in a Basket
observations: In the second vision, Zechariah sees a woman sitting in a basket, which represents wickedness being contained and removed from the land.
The basket is carried by two women with wings, symbolizing the swift removal of sin and evil from the community.
This vision emphasizes God's desire to purify His people and remove wickedness from their midst.

importantVerses.commentary: The curse that goes out over the land highlights the seriousness of sin and God's commitment to justice.
The removal of wickedness signifies God's active role in cleansing His people and restoring righteousness.

questions: What does the flying scroll symbolize in relation to God's judgment?
How does the vision of the woman in the basket reflect God's attitude towards sin?
What implications do these visions have for the community of believers today?
